question.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

current_example.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of $\mathbb{R}^3$ onto the subspace spanned by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154805/assets/30d85f2aa6f85a4a706a12a15d8d725b7c536f91316b51156290478eb8ceb1e2.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix $P_S = A(A^T\!A)^{-1}\!A^T$ maps any vector $\mathbf x\in \mathbb{R}^n$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154805/assets/1fe7fcc75295d4df8c2a2e92d87e2259c804620c25eb7f77647d9c579c142591.svg) Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\cdot (14)^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 2 & 4 & -6 \\ -3 & -6 & 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
